$comment: The pin manifest. A build is in this repository iff a TRACKED file of Archipelago-CC names it; scripts/procgen/check-seedling-wasm-pins.mjs in that repo gates the FOUR-way agreement between this manifest, the .gitignore whitelist, what git actually tracks here, and the build names that repo’s tracked files actually spell. Every build directory carries exactly four files. `js`/`wasm` are the AUTHORITY on the payload filenames — they do not always match the directory name. `capabilities` is the BUILD-SIDE HALF OF FEATURE DETECTION (⚖ user, 2026-08-29): the host decides from DATA whether a feature applies, never from an opt-in flag, so a build DECLARES what its ActionScript can do and the panel looks the entry up by the directory name its preset points at. It is MANDATORY and an empty array is a real answer — absence would be indistinguishable from “measured, none”. The vocabulary is declared ONCE, in the consumer (Archipelago-CC frontend/modules/flashPanel/seedlingRandomizerEligibility.js WASM_BUILD_CAPABILITIES), and check-seedling-wasm-pins.mjs imports it rather than spelling a second copy, so a typo cannot pass as “this build does not have it”. ⚖⚖ THE MANIFEST-PROSE EXEMPTION (ruled by the user 2026-08-30, EDITOR INTEGRATION slice P4): a gitlink bump whose submodule diff touches ONLY this file AND whose per-build payload md5s are byte-identical owes the pins gate plus the bounded reach, NOT the full-tier drive — the md5 identity is QUOTED in the outer commit as the licence. It is written where the OWED gate reads (Archipelago-CC scripts/procgen/check-seedling-full-tier-owed.mjs, which is what prices the tier) and restated here because this is the file the edit claiming it is made in. ⛔ THE BOUNDARY IS THE PREMISE, and it is all three clauses: touch a build directory, an md5 field or the .gitignore whitelist in the same commit and the exemption does not apply — a payload that moved is a different game, which is exactly what only the full tier can see. ⛓ `summary`, `role` and `source` (SEEDLING ORIGINAL WASM slice W2, ⚖ user 2026-09-07) ARE THE README'S BUILD TABLE, and the table is GENERATED from them — Archipelago-CC scripts/procgen/seedling-wasm-readme.mjs --write writes the `GENERATED:seedling-wasm-builds` region of README.md, and check-seedling-wasm-pins.mjs row (i) imports the same --check. `role` is one of demo / default / apitem-control / arm-control, the vocabulary declared ONCE in scripts/procgen/seedlingWasmReadme.js, and ⛔ the row does not stop at the spelling: it asks whether the LABEL IS TRUE OF THAT TREE — `default` must be the build WASM_PAGE names, `apitem-control` the build row (f)'s control drives, `demo` the entry declaring `demo: true`, `arm-control` a build that declares no `arm`. `source.commit` and `source.recompiler` are FULL 40-character SHAs because the table LINKS them: `builtFrom` abbreviated p4c's AS3 commit to seven characters and resolving it needed a clone of another repository. ⛔ THE PROSE FIELDS ARE NOT RENDERED — `builtFrom`, `namedBy` and `note` stay the long-form record and are read by people, not by the generator. The law itself now lives in docs/pin-policy.md; the retirements and the size policy in docs/history.md.

Object identity on FP.world is not a proxy for the observation's source: `FP.world as Game` feeds the dead-frame gate and findPlayer() is FP.world.classFirst(Player). ⚠ TWO OBSERVABLE CONSEQUENCES, both intended: the waiting frame is NOT counted in dead_frames (the tape has not started), so dead_frames on a swapping tape is the new world's fade alone — uniform, where p4b read that plus one on the winning path; and botStatus gains `arm: {pending, armed_at}`, the arm frame in Game.time units, which is what makes a driver-side arm bound's perturbation measurable at all. The RNG is unmoved: Rng.setState stays below the `new Game` line and the swap lands on the same frame as before.

builds.note: ⚖ THE DEMO BUILD, AND THE REASON THE PIN LAW GREW A SECOND CLAUSE (⚖ user, 2026-09-07, ruling 4). Every other build here is pinned because a tracked file of Archipelago-CC NAMES it — an instrument drives it. Nothing drives this one and nothing should: it is the game a person plays, at https://peerinfinity.github.io/seedling-wasm/seedling_original/game.html . So it is admitted by the other reason — `demo: true` HERE plus a link to `seedling_original/game.html` in THIS repo's README — and check-seedling-wasm-pins.mjs prints which reason admitted each build on every run. ⛔ THE README LINK IS THE LOAD-BEARING HALF: `demo: true` alone would be this manifest admitting itself. ⛓ `capabilities: []` IS A MEASUREMENT AND IT IS THE STRONGEST ONE IN THIS FILE. The vocabulary is `arm` and `apitem`, and both name ActionScript that only the FORK has: `arm` is the bot's world-swap arm time (fork branch `bot` @d4f1f37) and `apitem` is Archipelago's placement pickup (`ap-m1` @a0ec8642). This build is 826ba77 — the commit BEFORE the fork's first commit — so neither class exists in it, and `[]` is not "unmeasured", it is "this is the game before any of that". ⚠ It is therefore ALSO a second `arm`-less build, but row (g2) is deliberately NOT satisfied by it: (g2) asks for an `arm`-less build a tracked file can DRIVE, and nothing drives a demo. p4b remains the negative arm. ⛓ IT BOOTS WITH NO `__swfBridge` AND THE PAGE PROVES IT, MEASURED TWICE. Real-GPU Windows Chrome (intel/gen-9), the deployed game.html, one real click on the page's own ▶ Start: `__runtimeReady` at 0.5 s, 4,392 frames in 239.5 s (~18.3 fps), ⛔ 0 pageerrors, and exactly ONE console line naming the bridge — "[swfBridge] avm2 shim installed", the PAGE-side shim installing itself, with no `callback registered:` line after it (p4d's control run prints fifteen). The game's OWN trace() is the readiness signal rather than a harness timer: `Main.printItems()` prints "Level:" from `Main.begin()` at boot AND again from `Game.as:625` in the Game constructor, so the SECOND block — at 20.3 s — is the Splash ending and the playable world existing. The screenshot at 60 s is the title screen: "Seedling — press any key to play". ⚠ THE HEADLESS ARM CANNOT ANSWER THIS AND ITS RED IS NOT THIS BUILD'S: on WSL SwiftShader the same page reads 46 frames in 95 s (~0.5 fps, 36x slower, nowhere near the Splash's 450 frames) and 46 pageerrors of "A valid external Instance reference no longer exists", one per frame — and the CONTROL run of seedling_bot_ap_p4d, the shipped default, reads 46 frames and the SAME 46 pageerrors in the same window. A red the control shares is the rasteriser's, not the build's.
